description: Curated scientific corpus manifest for Darukaa BioIntel environmental intelligence system.

sources.title: Recarbonizing Global Soils: A Technical Manual of Recommended Management Practices
sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.summary: Technical guidelines by FAO on restoring soil organic carbon in degraded croplands and semi-arid drylands using conservation practices and legumes.
key_findings: In semi-arid drylands with baseline soil organic carbon below 0.5%, introducing legume-based cover crops and diversified agroforestry increases organic carbon retention and stimulates mycorrhizal activity without exacerbating water stress.
Under conservation management, soil organic carbon can increase at rates between 0.2 and 0.5 tonnes C/ha/year, with measurable gains observable over 2-3 years.
Leaving at least 30% crop residue on the surface combined with cover crops moderates soil temperature by 2-5 degrees Celsius and preserves soil moisture.

sources.title: Soil Organic Carbon: the hidden potential
sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.summary: FAO synthesis on the foundational role of soil organic carbon in biological diversity, soil physical stability, and hydrological resilience.
key_findings: In low-rainfall regions, each 1% increase in SOC can enhance available soil water capacity by up to 15-20 mm per meter of soil depth.
Depletion of SOC below 1.0% triggers a severe reduction in soil biological diversity, limiting enzymatic nutrient cycling.

sources.title: Soil Carbon Sequestration Impacts on Global Climate Change and Food Security
sources.summary: Landmark paper by Rattan Lal detailing carbon dynamics, rainfall use efficiency, and restoration of depleted dryland soils.
key_findings: Agricultural soils in dryland and semi-arid ecosystems contain severely depleted SOC pools, often less than 0.5%.
Adoption of restorative practices enhances rainfall use efficiency, reduces erosion, and rebuilds soil biological communities.
The critical threshold of SOC in low-rainfall regions is approximately 1.1% to prevent accelerated physical crusting and runoff.

sources.title: Climate Change and Land: Special Report on Climate Change, Desertification, Land Degradation
sources.summary: IPCC Special Report examining desertification, climate extremes, and sustainable land management in rainfed drylands.
key_findings: Continuous monoculture in semi-arid and arid zones exacerbates land degradation through soil organic matter depletion and wind erosion.
Sustainable land management practices, including intercropping, shelterbelts, and agroforestry, provide climate resilience by buffering microclimatic temperatures.
Trees on field boundaries lower ground-level wind speeds by 30-50%, curtailing topsoil loss and reducing plant transpiration stress.

sources.title: Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability. Chapter 5: Food, Fibre, and Other Ecosystem Products
sources.summary: IPCC AR6 WG2 Chapter 5 assessment on vulnerability of dryland cropping systems to rainfall deficits and heat stress.
key_findings: Polyculture rotations, hedgerow windbreaks, and mulching maintain soil humidity, lower surface evaporation by 20-30%, and stabilize yields under rainfall deficits.
Deploying drought-resilient legumes in crop rotations enhances nitrogen availability and dampens pest outbreaks during prolonged dry spells.

sources.title: Agricultural diversification promotes multiple ecosystem services without compromising yield
sources.summary: Global meta-analysis of 5,188 agricultural experiments showing diversification enhances biodiversity and soil organic carbon without reducing yields.
key_findings: Synthesis of 5,188 studies demonstrates that agricultural diversification enhances biodiversity by 24% and soil organic carbon by 6-15% without reducing crop yields.
Diversification strengthens pest regulation and pollination services simultaneously.
Homogeneous monocultures systematically diminish natural pest suppression and beneficial insect diversity.

sources.title: Agroforestry delivers a win-win solution for food security and ecosystem services
sources.summary: Meta-analysis documenting agroforestry impacts on dryland soil organic carbon, moisture retention, and biodiversity enhancement.
key_findings: Integrating nitrogen-fixing trees into dryland cropping systems improves nitrogen availability, enhances topsoil organic matter, and provides habitat for beneficial insects and birds.
Perennial boundary windbreaks lower crop water consumption by 15-20% and generate nesting refugia for predatory arthropods and pollinators.

sources.title: Mutually beneficial pollinator diversity and crop yield in small and large farms
sources.summary: Global cross-farm study in Science showing establishing native floral borders and hedgerows enhances wild pollinator diversity and stabilizes crop yields.
key_findings: Crop yield gaps can be closed by enhancing wild pollinator density and species richness through non-crop flowering borders and hedgerows.
Continuous agricultural monocultures devoid of semi-natural vegetation suffer pollinator deficits exceeding 50%.

sources.title: Biodiversity increases the resistance of ecosystem productivity to climate extremes
sources.summary: Nature study demonstrating that higher species richness provides critical ecosystem resistance and buffers productivity collapses during severe drought.
key_findings: Ecosystems with higher plant species richness sustain productivity during climate extremes, including severe drought.
Low diversity plant stands show half the resistance of high diversity stands during precipitation anomalies.

sources.title: Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
sources.publisher: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES)
sources.summary: Global landmark assessment by IPBES analyzing drivers of biodiversity loss and recommending ecological connectivity and multi-functional landscapes.
key_findings: Agricultural expansion and intensification without ecological corridors drive landscape fragmentation, pesticide pollution, and steep declines in terrestrial biodiversity.
Landscape-level connectivity established through native tree buffers and uncultivated boundary strips preserves ecological corridors and stabilizes ecosystem services.
